gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-anek-devanagari: Expressive and a bit wiry, Bushcraft spaces its letters far apart. Anek Devanagari is its opposite, a sans-serif with open mouths and a tall middle zone, and that gap between them is the pair's best card.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-anek-gujarati: Wide-set and single-minded, Bushcraft draws closed letters with no thick-thin flicker, while Anek Gujarati sits beside it as a sans-serif with a gaping c. Closed against open.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-anek-gurmukhi: Bushcraft draws closed, artistic letters with capitals that barely rise above the lowercase and plenty of space between them. Anek Gurmukhi, a sans-serif, does the opposite job: big open counters and generous curves in every small letter.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-anek-kannada: Anek Kannada reads contemporary and upright, its x-height reaching high with terminals stopping far from the stem. Bushcraft counters with closed letters, every stroke at one thickness, and that sharp difference in construction is the whole appeal.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-anek-latin: Artistic and spaced-out, Bushcraft looks thin everywhere because no part of its letters ever gets thinner than another. Anek Latin, a plain sans, stays open.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-anek-malayalam: Bushcraft looks drawn with a single tip, each glyph simple and closed. Its strongest quality is that simplicity, set against Anek Malayalam's curves whose ends never quite touch.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-anek-odia: Bushcraft's extra-wide spacing and its curves of unchanging weight are what you notice first, all closed shapes. It is strongest when showing off; Anek Odia, a sans, does best staying open and quiet.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-anek-telugu: Wide, wiry and artistic, Bushcraft closes its letters while Anek Telugu, a plain sans, leaves its rounds unsealed like an unlatched hook. Its wide, tall bowls would set a lively rhythm.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-anuphan: Bushcraft spreads its closed, artistic letters wide apart. Anuphan, a plain sans, feels rounder and more open beside it, with big bowls and curves that leave clear gaps.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-armata: Bushcraft traces its letters at a constant width, like a laser-etched line, and keeps them closed. Armata takes over below with spacious gaps and lowercase bodies filling most of the letter height.
